context.name: Context
context.audience: Anyone new to UNS, including non-engineers
context.blurb: UNS among the systems it talks to: the departments that send, the two GOV.UK Once systems it reads from and is read by, and the push provider that reaches a phone. C4 level 1 — runtime only.
context.note: Nothing here is derived from CloudFormation. UNS's CDK app imports a package that only a private registry serves, so this page is read from the source and every count on it is prose.

send.name: Send path
send.audience: On-call, and anyone tracing a notification that did not arrive
send.blurb: A message from a department to a phone, hop by hop, and beside it the group form of the same thing. Both share the dispatch queue and everything after it; the group path never asks UDP, because a group is already a list of push ids.
send.note: Every queue adds a ten-second delivery delay, so the fastest single message spends twenty seconds in queues before OneSignal sees it. A fresh environment deploys with both adapters set to VOID and sends nothing until SSM says otherwise.
send.dashMeans: a read or write of state beside the path, not a hop the message takes

containers.name: Containers
containers.audience: UNS engineers, and anyone reviewing a change to the stack
containers.blurb: Every separately deployable part the CDK app creates per environment, grouped by the construct tree that owns it. One stack holds everything; a second holds the alarms. C4 level 2.
containers.note: Feature-flagged parts — the group store, the group queue, the group functions — exist in development and staging and not in production. Edges to the analytics queue are omitted: every function sends to it.

components.name: Components
components.audience: Engineers changing a handler — this is the code, not the infrastructure
components.blurb: Inside one HTTP Lambda: the four middleware groups every handler runs through, in order, and the services the handler is handed. Queue and schedule handlers have shorter chains, drawn as single boxes. C4 level 3.
components.note: Dependencies are resolved inside the handler on every invocation, so a cold start pays nothing for them and a warm one pays every time.
components.dashMeans: a hand-off inside the library, not a call the handler makes

flex.name: Read-back API
flex.audience: FLEX engineers, and anyone tracing what the app sees
flex.blurb: What FLEX reads and changes on the app's behalf: a person's notifications, and the groups their device belongs to. Numbered from the caller down.
flex.note: The person is a query-string id, the same push id UDP returned on the send path. A status change is an analytics event, not a write: what the app reads next depends on the analytics function having run.
flex.dashMeans: a secret read out of band, not a request

network.name: Network
network.audience: Anyone changing a subnet, an endpoint or a security group
network.blurb: One VPC per main environment, two tiers, and which functions are in it. Most are not: the HTTP handlers run outside the VPC; only the pipeline functions and the cache are inside.
network.note: There is no isolated tier. The functions inside the VPC have a route to the internet through the NAT gateways, which is how OneSignal and UDP are reached.

security.name: Security
security.audience: Security review, on-call, and anyone answering an audit question
security.blurb: The controls that bound every box on the other tabs, in five columns: who may call, what is encrypted and with which key, what records, what wakes someone, and what survives.
security.note: Development is a main environment: it keeps logs for a year, retains its resources, and issues certificates from its own CA like production does.
security.dashMeans: a relation between two controls, not a call

delivery.name: Delivery
delivery.audience: Anyone shipping a change, and on-call
delivery.blurb: Three zones: what a pull request gets, what a merge to main ships and where it stops, and the things outside the repository every run depends on. Every step is a GitHub Actions job; read each zone top to bottom.
delivery.note: Staging and production both wait for the dev job — which includes the end-to-end tests — and not for each other. Nothing in the YAML holds production back further.
delivery.dashMeans: a trigger or an out-of-band read, not a job dependency

resources.name: Resources
resources.audience: Cost, audit and incident scoping — the detail behind every badge
resources.blurb: Every AWS resource the CDK app declares, counted per environment by reading the constructs.
resources.note: Counts follow the stage selector, and every one of them is read from the source rather than derived from synthesised templates: the CDK app imports once-platform-constructs from a private CodeArtifact registry, which this pipeline cannot reach. A read role for that registry is what it would take to bind these numbers to a synth. Consumer-dependent rows count the organisations named in code for that environment.
